title: Set off and counter claim - underused defensive tools
p1:
What if you could reduce the amount you owe in a lawsuit without simply defending yourself?

Many people overlook two powerful legal tools: set-off and counterclaim. They can change the direction of a dispute entirely.
p2:
A common misconception is that when someone files a claim against you, your only option is to challenge their allegations.

That's not always true.

A set-off allows you to account for money the other party also owes you. A counterclaim goes a step further: it allows you to bring your own claim against the person who sued you, within the same proceedings where permitted.
p3:
Here's a practical example:

A supplier demands $20,000 for unpaid invoices, but you have a valid $7,000 claim against them for defective goods.

Depending on the applicable law and circumstances, a set-off may reduce the amount payable. A counterclaim could allow you to seek additional relief for the loss you suffered.

The key insight? A defendant may have a claim of their own, not just a defence.

Identifying these possibilities early can strengthen your legal strategy, avoid unnecessary proceedings, and improve settlement discussions. The rules and availability of each remedy depend on the jurisdiction and nature of the claims.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a defendant overlook a valid set-off or counterclaim and focus entirely on defending the original lawsuit? Which tool do you think is more frequently underused?
